source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Lebanon, Ohio campus publishes 35 MW of IT capacity, the largest published figure of any facility mapped in a state where only 9 of 79 sites publish a megawatt figure at all.

That gap is the real finding. Ohio has 79 mapped data centers and 9 published power figures summing to 118.4 MW, so this single campus is close to 30 percent of the state's known total. Most of Ohio's data center footprint is invisible at the level of power, which means any state-level capacity estimate rests on a handful of disclosures.

The 35 MW is a power figure, not a rack count. At 40 kW per rack, a common density for AI training halls, 35 MW works out to roughly 875 racks, but that is an assumption about density rather than anything CyrusOne states. The campus has 400,000 square feet of technical space and the power to fill it, and the operator has not published which accelerators, if any, are deployed there.

The certifications, SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and Green Globes, qualify the campus for specific classes of work but name no tenant. The spec page publishes no tenants, pricing, or interconnection details. This campus matters as a power asset in a state where published power is scarce, and whether AI workloads actually run there is not published.
